title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' (modérée) geometry, the programme of Esquisse §5. In it, figures (subspaces) of a space X are built from 'elementary figures', for example convex cells or simplices (the margin says 'ingrédients' ('convexes')). Page 8 has just shown that a figure F is determined by the set Φ = Σ'_F of elementary pieces it contains, and has characterized such sets: (a) closed under the order, (b) pairwise compatible, (c) locally finite. Page 9 now abstracts this into a purely combinatorial structure. (1) A set F_el of elementary figures. (2) A partial order ≤ on F_el, meaning inclusion of figures. (3) A reflexive symmetric relation R, 'F and G are compatible'. Geometrically this presumably means that F ∩ G is a common face, as in a polyhedral complex. A configuration is a subset of F_el whose elements are pairwise compatible, i.e. a clique of the compatibility graph. (4) Among configurations, a distinguished family Conf_l.f. ⊂ P(F_el) of 'locally finite' ones, required to behave like an antifiltre (an ideal of subsets). The axioms are: (a) singletons are locally finite; (b) a configuration is locally finite iff a related set formed using the order ≤ is locally finite (garbled; perhaps its ≤-saturation, or a finiteness condition on elements below each given element); (c) any subset Ψ of a locally finite configuration is locally finite; (d) if a configuration is a finite union of locally finite configurations, it is locally finite. The next page then defines a figure as a configuration that is downward closed for ≤. Finite figures are the finite such subsets. It also adds the compatibility axiom Fig_1: two elements below a common element are compatible. So the down-set of any elementary figure is a figure, which gives the embedding of F_el into figures. The problem served is to get a combinatorial, poset-theoretic presentation of the category of 'tame' figures of a space, independent of point-set topology. It is essentially an abstract polyhedral complex: a face poset plus a compatibility relation plus a local-finiteness ideal. This would replace triangulations and point-set topology.
errors: Axiom (b) on locally finite configurations is illegible/garbled, so its exact content cannot be verified; as transcribed it is incomplete.

The compatibility of a figure with its subfigures (x ≤ y, x' ≤ y ⇒ x R x') is not stated on this page. It is only added on p.10 as Fig_1. Without it, the down-set of an elementary figure need not be a configuration, so the structure on p.9 alone is insufficient to recover elementary figures as figures.

Axiom (d) needs the finite-union hypothesis (an arbitrary union of locally finite sets need not be locally finite); the transcription's '(réunion finie[?])' should be kept. With it, (c)+(d) make Conf_l.f. an ideal ('antifiltre') restricted to cliques, consistent with the stated intent.

ideas.what: Presenting figures of a tame space by a poset of elementary figures with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation; configurations = pairwise-compatible subsets; figures = downward-closed configurations
ideas.modern_name: abstract polyhedral/cell complex via face poset; clique (flag) complex of a compatibility graph; cliques of a coherence space (web with reflexive symmetric relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: abstract simplicial/cell complexes: classical (Alexandrov, Tucker, etc.); coherence spaces: J.-Y. Girard 1986-87
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces 'topologie modérée' but does not give this combinatorial axiomatization

ideas.what: Locally finite configurations forming an 'antifiltre' (ideal) in P(F_el), with axioms: singletons, hereditary, closed under finite unions that remain configurations
ideas.modern_name: bornology / ideal of 'small' subsets; locally finite families as in CW/polyhedral complexes

ideas.what: Recovering a (possibly infinite) figure uniquely from its set of elementary pieces (from p.8), making figures a combinatorial object
ideas.modern_name: cell decomposition / face-poset reconstruction in o-minimal or PL geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)

missed.claim: The structure (set + reflexive symmetric 'compatibility' relation, with configurations = pairwise compatible subsets) is exactly Girard's coherence space and its cliques, written almost simultaneously (1986). Grothendieck enriches it with an order and an ideal of locally finite cliques, to model geometric figures.
missed.quote: relation symétrique réflexive R "F et G compatibles" — Configuration (élémentaire) : partie de F_el formée d'él. deux à deux compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a curiosity rather than a deep link. It suggests tame-topological figures could be treated as (ordered) coherence-space/clique-complex data, connecting combinatorial models of o-minimal or PL geometry with the clique-based structures used in linear logic and in flag complexes.

missed.claim: An intrinsic, point-free combinatorial axiomatization of 'tame' figures was begun here: a poset of elementary figures, a compatibility relation and a local-finiteness ideal. It was never published and was not developed into a theory of tame spaces.
missed.quote: Ainsi, on est arrivé à la structure suivante ① F_el ... ② relation d'ordre ... ③ relation symétrique réflexive R ... ④ ... loc. finies ... propriétés d'antifiltre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The Esquisse's 'topologie modérée' was later read mainly through o-minimality. This page shows Grothendieck pursuing instead a combinatorial-presentation approach, closer to face posets and abstract polyhedral complexes. That alternative axiomatics is little documented.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished glimpse of how Grothendieck concretely tried to axiomatize the tame topology of the Esquisse: abstract elementary figures, compatibility, and locally finite configurations. The individual notions are elementary and close to standard abstract complexes, so the novelty lies in the documented approach rather than in any result.
transcription_corrections: Item ④: the inserted words read as 'dynamique de l'ens.' are dubious; the line essentially says 'Parmi les configurations, celles qui sont "loc. finies", avec propriétés d'antifiltre'.
Axiom d) should read roughly: 'Si Φ est une configuration, Φ = ∪Φ_i (réunion finie) où les Φ_i sont loc. finies, alors Φ est loc. finie'.
Axiom c) reads roughly: 'si Φ est une configuration loc. finie, toute Ψ ⊂ Φ est loc. finie'.

The left-margin notes are oblique and largely illegible. The lower one mentions 'les "ingrédients" ("convexes")', and the bottom-left word may be 'X fini'/'X compact' rather than part of the main text; the transcription's reading of the upper margin ('donc une configuration est...') is uncertain.
